tasks.short: Implement supply chain process improvements and assess their operational results.

steps.what: Collect transaction histories, service measures and process costs.
Walk the process with operational teams and identify causes of delays or waste.
Compare improvement options, implementation costs and expected service effects.
Agree the pilot scope, resources, success measures and rollback conditions.
Configure approved process rules for the pilot scope.
Run the pilot and resolve operational problems with affected teams.
Assess pilot results against the baseline and recommend expansion, revision or rollback.

tasks.design: A reusable scenario calculator accepts file imports, then connects {OPS_SYSTEM} and {ERP} through {DATA_PLATFORM} to build comparable baselines. Configure pilot approvals and versioned rules in {WORKFLOW}; a {BI} view compares outcomes while people diagnose causes, authorize changes and run pilots.
tasks.previous_blocker: Process definitions and cost measures differed across teams. Building each comparison and connecting operational records took scarce analyst time.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of building adapters, scenario calculators and repeatable checks. Existing configuration handles many process-rule changes.
tasks.still_hard: A pilot can disrupt service. Changes in demand, staffing or product mix can obscure whether the intervention caused the result.
tasks.human_edge: Recognize informal workarounds, earn staff cooperation and judge which operational trade-offs are acceptable.

ambition.what: Fortnightly selection of the next bottleneck pilot using comparable results.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from assembling evidence toward observing operations and running focused trials. The manager gains faster recommendations; spending and rollout rights remain subject to existing delegation.

reach.task: Define pilot milestones, dependencies and rollback checkpoints.
reach.learn: Small-pilot design, dependency mapping and benefit attribution.

reach.task: Validate that a process change preserves quality controls.
reach.learn: Control plans and evidence needed before expanding a pilot.

evidence.claim: Baseline extraction, scenario calculations and pilot tracking can use deterministic integrations and workflow configuration.
Forecasting and inventory configuration are established improvement tools; Slim4 is documented for these functions.

assumptions: The first release covers one process and one pilot site.
Time shares and remaining effort are planning estimates, informed by the supplied priors.
Analysis uses aggregate process measures rather than individual worker scoring.
Access and consultation estimates include employee consultation where national rules require it; formal procedures can take longer.
unknowns: Which process is the first pilot and who can authorize its changes?
Are transaction timestamps and cost allocations reliable enough for a baseline?
Which process rules can be configured without changing operational software?
Which national consultation requirements apply to the proposed work redesign?
research_questions: Which comparison method best separates pilot effects from seasonal demand and product-mix changes?
new_work: Maintain event mappings and cost definitions.
Review failed imports and implausible scenario assumptions.
Check pilot configuration and rollback readiness.
Review whether observed benefits persist after expansion.

tasks.short: Develop and agree procedures connecting supply chain work with other functions.

steps.what: Collect existing procedures, handoff failures and departmental requirements.
Resolve conflicting priorities and agree responsibilities, triggers and escalation paths.
Draft the procedure, responsibility table and exception instructions.

loop.input: Approved template, source procedures and recorded handoff decisions.
loop.output: Draft procedure with source references and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Validate required sections and role names; reviewers check every responsibility and exception against recorded decisions.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unresolved conflicts return to functional leads before approval.
loop.why_not_simpler: A template supplies structure, but varied prose needs interpretation to express the agreed handoffs clearly.

steps.what: Approve responsibilities, service commitments and exceptions in the proposed procedure.
Set up handoff forms, routing rules, deadlines and escalation notifications.
Publish the approved procedure and retire superseded versions.

tasks.design: Configure structured requirement collection in {WORKFLOW} and versioned procedure templates in {DOCS}. A bounded drafting loop turns recorded decisions into a referenced draft; functional leads approve commitments before configured handoffs become active and the approved version is published.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requirements arrived in inconsistent messages, and document approval was separate from workflow setup. Departmental disagreement could not be solved by routing rules.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable forms and approval configuration handle collection and publication. A bounded model loop can turn varied source prose into a reviewable procedure draft.
tasks.still_hard: Departments must agree who bears delays, costs and exceptions. A published procedure can still fail if teams lack capacity or incentives to follow it.
tasks.human_edge: Negotiate workable commitments and notice when formal responsibilities conflict with how teams actually operate.

ambition.what: Monthly revision of one recurring cross-functional handoff failure.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time chasing inputs and formatting procedures, and more time resolving disputed handoffs. Functional leads retain approval of their commitments; no unilateral authority is gained.

reach.task: Map departmental handoffs and test the proposed procedure against exception cases.
reach.learn: Process mapping, responsibility design and scenario-based procedure review.

reach.task: Maintain publication, acknowledgement and escalation arrangements.
reach.learn: Document version control and practical adoption measures.

evidence.claim: Forms, approval routing and versioned publication can be configured without autonomous agents.
A bounded drafting loop can prepare procedures from supplied decisions, with human review of commitments.

assumptions: The first release covers one cross-functional procedure.
Existing templates and approval roles can be reused.
The loop receives recorded decisions rather than inferring agreement from informal discussion.
Access and consultation estimates include national procedures where responsibilities or working arrangements change.
unknowns: Who must approve each departmental commitment?
Which procedures already have formal document controls?
Can handoff routing use maintained role groups?
Do national rules require employee consultation for the intended changes?
research_questions: Which draft checks most reliably detect omitted exceptions and invented responsibilities?
new_work: Review generated procedures against source decisions.
Maintain role groups, escalation paths and templates.
Resolve incomplete submissions and conflicting requirements.
Check that published instructions match active workflow rules.

tasks.short: Agree demand forecasts and feasible supply plans with planners.

steps.what: Assemble demand history, open orders, stock positions and supply commitments.
Prepare forecast adjustments and supply scenarios against capacity and lead-time constraints.
Discuss demand changes, shortages and scenario assumptions with planners.
Choose service priorities, forecast overrides and the feasible supply plan.
Record the approved plan and overrides in operational planning records.

tasks.design: A reusable planning view imports files or joins {ERP}, {OPS_SYSTEM} and {CRM} through {DATA_PLATFORM}. Configure available forecasting and constraint features in {OPS_SYSTEM}, expose exceptions in {BI}, and write back only the approved planning version with recorded override reasons.
tasks.previous_blocker: Snapshots used different cut-off times and planners reconciled scenarios by hand. Demand shifts and scarce capacity still required discussion.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing forecasting features can supply baselines, while cheaper adapters and validation code make a shared planning snapshot easier to build.
tasks.still_hard: Promotions, new products and uncertain supplier commitments weaken forecasts. Capacity models can omit real production constraints.
tasks.human_edge: Challenge commercial optimism, interpret weak signals and negotiate which customers or products receive scarce supply.

ambition.what: Daily shortage-priority decisions between scheduled planning meetings.

tasks.altitude: Planners arrive with checked scenarios, so the manager spends meetings on assumptions and allocation choices. Existing approval limits remain; faster evidence supports decisions within those limits.

reach.task: Check that the approved supply plan can become an executable production schedule.
reach.learn: Capacity calendars, material dependencies and frozen scheduling periods.

reach.task: Backtest forecasts and examine service effects of overrides.
reach.learn: Forecast bias, stockout-censored demand and override evaluation.

evidence.claim: Slim4 forecasts demand and sets stock by item and location.
Shared snapshots, constraint checks and approved-plan write-back can use deterministic technology.

assumptions: The first release covers one product family and planning horizon.
The target planning module supports baseline forecasts and the required basic constraints.
Spreadsheet scenario work is a typical cross-system bridge, although some companies already perform it in {OPS_SYSTEM}.
Plan release changes internal planning records; purchase orders and customer promises follow separate authorization.
No individual worker scoring is introduced.
unknowns: Which forecasting and constraint features are already licensed and used?
How are lost sales, substitutions and exceptional orders recorded?
Who can approve allocation changes and forecast overrides?
Are supplier commitments and capacity calendars maintained?
What access approvals or national consultation requirements apply?
research_questions: Which forecast baseline performs best by demand pattern and planning horizon?
How should scenario evaluation account for demand hidden by stockouts?
new_work: Resolve stale snapshots and failed plan imports.
Maintain capacity constraints and lead-time assumptions.
Review forecast bias and the effects of overrides.
Check that write-back preserves approval status and planning versions.

tasks.short: Analyze inventory and choose actions that balance turns, waste and customer service.

steps.what: Extract stock, demand, movements and inventory valuation at a common cut-off.
Reconcile item codes, units, valuation differences and missing movement records.
Calculate turns, ageing, service levels and alternative stock-policy outcomes.
Validate apparent excesses and shortages with warehouse and planning teams.
Choose stock-policy changes and assign excess-stock or service-recovery actions.
Review whether assigned actions improve stock, waste and service measures.

tasks.design: A reusable calculator starts with inventory file imports, then joins {OPS_SYSTEM} and {ERP} in {DATA_PLATFORM} with explicit reconciliation rules. A {BI} dashboard shows ageing, service trade-offs and stock-policy scenarios; {WORKFLOW} tracks approved actions and subsequent results.
tasks.previous_blocker: Inventory and financial records used different definitions and cut-offs. Repeat analysis required manual joins, while the reasons behind exceptional stock remained local knowledge.
tasks.enabler_now: Deterministic calculations and configurable inventory features already exist. AI-assisted coding makes reusable mappings, reconciliation checks and scenario views cheaper to assemble.
tasks.still_hard: Recorded demand can hide lost sales, and high turns can accompany poor availability. Obsolete stock, strategic buffers and unreliable suppliers need contextual judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguish unnecessary stock from deliberate resilience and balance cash release against customer harm.
tasks.altitude: The week shifts from reconciling reports toward choosing interventions and checking their effects. The manager gains a stronger basis for recommendations; write-offs and policy changes remain within existing approval limits.

reach.task: Investigate stock discrepancies before they influence policy recommendations.
reach.learn: Cycle-count controls, stock status codes and movement reconciliation.

reach.task: Evaluate inventory-policy alternatives against service and working-capital outcomes.
reach.learn: Demand segmentation, safety-stock assumptions and comparable outcome measures.

evidence.claim: Slim4 supports forecasts and stock settings by item and location.
The Lasaulec vendor case reports stock falling over 20% with availability above 98%; the period is unspecified.
Reconciliation, ageing metrics and stock-policy scenarios can be calculated deterministically; local outcomes require validation.

assumptions: The first release covers one inventory scope with agreed metric definitions.
No case-study result is treated as a forecast of customer savings.
Recommendations do not automatically dispose of stock, release purchases or change customer commitments.
Data access follows GDPR requirements where records contain personal data.
Access estimates include required reviews; national consultation requirements depend on the actual deployment.
unknowns: Can stock quantities and values be reconciled at the same cut-off?
Are quarantine, consignment and reserved stock identified consistently?
Are waste, lost sales and service failures recorded reliably?
Who approves stock-policy changes and inventory write-offs?
Which access or employee consultation requirements apply?
research_questions: Which inventory segments need separate service and stock-policy models?
How should evaluation distinguish deliberate resilience stock from avoidable excess?
new_work: Resolve unmatched items, units and stock statuses.
Maintain metric definitions and stock-policy assumptions.
Review false alerts and data-quality exceptions.
Track action outcomes and detect service deterioration.

role.altitude: The manager spends more of the week testing operational changes, challenging assumptions and negotiating service trade-offs. Faster evidence supports more frequent decisions within existing authority; additional spending or cross-functional powers require explicit delegation.
reach: Work with logistics analysts on scenario quality and outcome measurement.
Work with production planning staff on feasible schedules and constraints.
Work with quality managers and project specialists on controlled pilots and rollout decisions.
skills_to_grow: Translate operational questions into explicit data definitions and constraints.
Interpret forecasts, uncertainty and service-versus-stock trade-offs.
Design pilots that distinguish intervention effects from background changes.
Negotiate cross-functional commitments and workable exception paths.
Review integrations, approvals and data-quality controls.
role.ambitious_version: Run a recurring supply chain improvement service that gives operational teams checked scenarios, small pilot plans and measured results, while people retain consequential operational decisions.
